title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: The Statement Cycle Examined for Excess Withdrawal Fees
content:
Squaring a Savings & Money Market Accounts product's excess withdrawal fees with its counted withdrawals is done one Statement Cycle at a time. This page defines which Statement Cycle that is and the calendar conditions under which the work is done.

## Rule

**Anchor entry.** The anchor is the account's latest overdraft protection transfer, that is, of the withdrawals made through the overdraft transfer channel, the one posted most recently.

**Receiving account.** The anchor serves only where the money went to a Personal Checking account held by the same customer, namely the checking account whose shortfall it covered. Where the receiving account is anything else, the policy squares nothing.

**Shared latest date.** Where overdraft protection transfers to two or more different accounts all posted on that latest date, the ledger cannot show which of them came last, and the policy squares nothing.

**The Statement Cycle.** The Statement Cycle examined is the one the anchor transfer belongs to.

## Calendar conditions

The work is done only when both of the following are borne out by the records; the fee figure itself does not test them:

- the Statement Cycle examined is the one now running, the one that will close on the account's next closing date, judged from the current date and the account's statement closing day;
- the current date, being the day of the contact, is a business day: a weekday that is not a Federal Reserve holiday. Anything posted during the contact, including a fee written under this policy, then carries the current date and falls inside that Statement Cycle.

If either fails, the policy squares nothing.

## Hypothetical cases

- The account's Statement Cycle closes on the 20th. Today is Tuesday 8 July, and the latest overdraft protection transfer, to the owner's checking account, belongs to the Statement Cycle closing 20 July. That Statement Cycle is examined.
- Same account, but the latest overdraft protection transfer belongs to the Statement Cycle that closed on 20 June. That is not the one now running, so the policy squares nothing.
- The call falls on a Sunday. The policy squares nothing that day.
